optional_codes.reason: Personal history of other diseases of the respiratory system, for the asthma he had as a child: a history code may be added, nothing requires it, and the provider draws no connection between the old asthma and this illness. Defensible either way.

unsupported_codes.reason: Asthma: reporting a code from this category treats asthma as a current condition. The note records it only as a condition he had as a child, with no symptoms and no inhalers since age 12, and the provider's diagnosis is acute bronchitis.

citations.J20.9: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section IV.J: code all documented conditions that coexist at the time of the visit and that require or affect patient care, treatment or management; do not code conditions that were previously treated and no longer exist; history codes may be used as secondary codes if the historical condition has an impact on current care or influences treatment. Section I.A.19: the assignment of a diagnosis code is based on the provider's diagnostic statement that the condition exists. Category J20 includes acute bronchitis with bronchospasm. Here the emergency physician's diagnosis is acute bronchitis; asthma appears only in the history, as a condition of childhood with no symptoms and no inhalers since age 12, and the physician does not diagnose asthma, so acute bronchitis is reported and asthma is not reported as a current condition.

coder_notes: Wheezes that clear with albuterol suggest reactive airways, but naming asthma from that is a conclusion the provider has not written. Wheezing and cough are part of the acute bronchitis. No organism is identified. He has never smoked. The inhaler is a one-week, as-needed prescription.
